environment.description: Application deployed identically but fronted by Google Cloud Armor security policy 'corp-prod-policy' attached to an external HTTPS L7 load balancer. The policy has two rules evaluated in priority order: (1) Priority 1000: preconfiguredWafRules with expression 'evaluatePreconfiguredWaf(sqli-v33-stable, {sensitivity: 1})' action DENY(403). (2) Priority 2000: preconfiguredWafRules with expression 'evaluatePreconfiguredWaf(xss-v33-stable, {sensitivity: 1})' action DENY(403). Additionally, the backend service has Cloud IAP (Identity-Aware Proxy) enabled requiring Google OAuth authentication with audience restriction to the project's OAuth client ID, meaning unauthenticated requests never reach the application. The combination means: even if an authenticated internal user attempts SQLi, Cloud Armor's ModSecurity CRS 3.3 SQLi ruleset at sensitivity level 1 (paranoia level 1) inspects the full request URI including query parameters and blocks common UNION-based and boolean-based injection patterns before they reach the backend.

config.cloud_iap: enabled, OAuth client audience restricted to project
config.firewall_rule: allow ingress tcp:8080 from GCP health-check ranges and L7 LB proxy subnet only
